extracted.intended_audience: ARIPO member state officials, national IP office staff, IP policymakers, patent and trademark attorneys, and stakeholders engaged in regional IP administration
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed amendments to the Harare Protocol (patents, utility models, industrial designs) and the Banjul Protocol (trademarks) setting substantive and procedural standards for filing, examination, rights, ownership, electronic processing, fees and relations with international treaties. Targets how ARIPO and designated national offices should process and treat regional applications and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble — inclusion of Paris Convention and PCT references
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend the preamble to include reference to Article 19 of the Paris Convention and a Regional Treaty within the meaning of Article 45(1) of the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: The preamble should explicitly include the Paris Convention and PCT Articles to link the Harare Protocol to these international instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and effect of ARIPO rights (Section 1(2) and 1(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents granted or utility models and industrial designs registered by virtue of this Protocol shall respectively be called ARIPO patents, ARIPO utility models and ARIPO industrial designs; the ARIPO right shall, in each contracting state for which it is granted or registered, have the effect of, and be subject to the same conditions as, a national patent/utility model/industrial design of that state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: New paragraphs 2 and 3 clearly define ARIPO rights and their effect relative to Member States' national rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial effect — request for one or more states (Section 1bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant of an ARIPO patent or the registration of an ARIPO utility model or industrial design may be requested for one or more of the contracting states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Confirms that ARIPO rights can have effect in any subset of contracting states designated in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint applicants designating different states (Section 2(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent, utility model or industrial design application may be filed by joint applicants or by two or more applicants designating different contracting states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Facilitates applications by joint applicants designating different contracting states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of applications (Section 2(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an ARIPO patent, utility model or industrial design can be lodged in any language which must be translated into English within two (2) months from the date of filing in accordance with Rule 5(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Supports Rule 5(2) — allows lodging in any language but requires English translation within two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority — entitlement and periods (Section 2(8)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who has duly filed in a Paris Convention state or a WTO member an application for a patent, utility model or industrial design (or successor in title) shall enjoy a right of priority of 12 months for patents and utility models and 6 months for industrial designs from the date of the first filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Clarifies entitlement to priority and the applicable priority periods for different IP types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority — recognition, declaration, and multiple priorities (Section 2(8)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Every filing equivalent to a regular national filing under national law or under bilateral/multilateral agreements (including this Protocol) shall be recognized as giving rise to priority. (b) Applicant desiring priority must file a declaration of priority and any documents required by implementing regulations. (c) Multiple priorities may be claimed, even if originating in different countries; where multiple priorities are claimed, time limits run from the earliest date of priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Defines forms of recognized priority, procedural requirements to claim it, and treatment of multiple priorities (including that time limits run from earliest priority date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single invention / linked inventions requirement (Section 3(1A))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Ensures unity of invention — single invention or linked group forming one inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure / enablement (Section 3(1B))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application must disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Requires enablement so a skilled person can reproduce or carry out the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims clarity, conciseness and support (Section 3(1C))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims shall define the matter for which protection is sought; they shall be clear and concise and be supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Claims must be interpretable, not ambiguous, and must have basis in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract purpose (Section 3(1D))
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall merely serve for use as technical information; in particular not for the purpose of interpreting the scope of the protection sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Abstracts are for technical information only and should not be used to construe claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical and formal requirements; filing date accord (Section 3(2A))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall examine whether the formal and physical requirements for the applications as laid down in the Regulations and Administrative Instructions have been complied with and shall accord the appropriate filing date to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Need to link physical requirements to the Administrative Instructions; office must verify compliance before assigning filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member States' right to accept or refuse grant (Section 3(6A))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office decides to grant the patent, it shall notify the applicant and each designated State, attaching any search or examination report; each designated State shall have six (6) months within which to respond to the notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Provides Member States the opportunity to accept or refuse a patent granted or due for grant by ARIPO; old Section 3(6) re-numbered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty cross-reference amendment (Section 3(7) amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-numbered Section 3(7) should be amended to refer to sub-section 3(6) (correction of a cross-reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Corrects internal references so novelty provisions point to the correct subsection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty definition (Section 3(11A))
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be considered to be new if it is not anticipated by the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Clear statement that novelty requires absence of anticipation in prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of prior art (Section 3(11B))
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything made available to the public anywhere in the world by written disclosure (including drawings), oral disclosure, use or exhibition, shall be considered prior art if made before the filing date or valid priority date; a disclosure at an official exhibition is excluded if it occurred not more than six months before filing/priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Broad definition of prior art including oral and use; six-month exhibition exception aligned with many national rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: International exhibition definition (Section 3(11C))
rubrics_metrics.description: An official or officially recognized exhibition is an exhibition recognized by a State or falling within the Convention on International Exhibitions (Paris 1928, revised 1972).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Links exhibition exception to the Convention's definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (Section 3(11D))
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be considered as involving an inventive step if, having regard to the prior art, it is not obvious to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Standard non-obviousness test phrased in terms of a person skilled in the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability (Section 3(11E))
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be considered as susceptible of industrial applicability if it can be made or utilized in any kind of industry including agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Defines 'industrial applicability' broadly to include agriculture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to application/limits on added subject-matter (Section 3(11F))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant shall be allowed at least one opportunity to amend the description, claims and drawings of his own volition; an ARIPO patent application or patent may not be amended so as to contain subject-matter extending beyond the content of the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Permits at least one voluntary amendment but prohibits addition of new matter beyond original filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing ARIPO applications/rights by territory (Section 3(13A))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application may be licensed in whole or in part for the whole or part of the territories of the designated Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Allows territorially-partitioned licensing of regional applications/rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments — formal requirements (Section 3(13B))
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment of an ARIPO patent application shall be made in writing and shall require the signature of the parties to the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Sets signature and writing requirements for assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership — inventor and employee rules (Section 3(14A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Right to an ARIPO patent shall belong to the inventor or his successor in title; if the inventor is an employee, the right shall be determined in accordance with the law of the state in which the employee is mainly employed; if that state cannot be determined, apply the law of the state where the employer has a place of business to which the employee is attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Establishes choice-of-law rules for employee-inventor ownership disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership — simultaneous independent inventors (Section 3(14B))
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more persons have made the same invention independently, the right to an ARIPO patent shall belong to the person whose patent application has the earliest filing date, provided that this first application has been published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: First-to-file rule subject to publication of the earliest application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of grant — rights conferred (Section 3(14C))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent shall confer on its proprietor from the date on which the mention of its grant is published in the ARIPO Journal, in each contracting state in respect of which it is granted, the same rights as would be conferred by a national patent granted in that state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Publication of grant in ARIPO Journal triggers national-equivalent rights in designated states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional protection upon publication (Section 3(14D))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application shall on the date of its publication provisionally confer upon the applicant the protection provided for in Section 3(14C) in the contracting states designated in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Publication of application grants provisional protection equivalent to that described for granted patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement governed by national law (Section 3(14E))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any infringement of any ARIPO patent shall be dealt with by the national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Enforcement/remedies are matters for national courts and laws of designated states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications — filing, scope and priority (Section 3(15A))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO divisional application shall be filed directly with the ARIPO Office in accordance with the implementing regulations; it may be filed only in respect of subject matter which does not extend beyond the scope of an earlier application as filed; if complied with, the divisional shall be filed on the date of filing of the earlier application and enjoy the same right of priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Divisional applications must stay within original disclosure and can enjoy the parent's filing date and priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional designation propagation (Section 3(15B))
rubrics_metrics.description: All contracting states designating the earlier application at the time of filing of an ARIPO divisional application shall be deemed to be designated in the divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Ensures territorial designations of the parent carry over to divisionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning and interpretation of claims (Section 3(16))
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of the protection conferred by an ARIPO patent or ARIPO application shall be determined by the terms of the claims; nevertheless, the description and drawings shall be used to interpret the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Claims define scope but description/drawings assist interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and Administrative Instructions (Section 3(17))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Instructions shall specify: (i) time limits to be observed in proceedings before the ARIPO Office not fixed by the Protocol; (ii) manner of computation of time limits and conditions under which time limits may be extended; (iii) the minima and maxima for the time limits to be determined by the ARIPO Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Delegates detailed timing rules, computation and extension mechanisms to Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation or invalidation effects (Section 3(18))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application and the resulting patent shall be deemed not to have had, as from the outset, the effects specified in (14B) and (14C) to the extent that the patent has been revoked in opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Provides that revocation/invalidation removes retroactive effects of grant as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link to Hague Agreement for industrial designs (New Section 4bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a link between the Harare Protocol and the Hague Agreement to facilitate filing of international industrial designs; ARIPO to join/ratify the Hague System for the international registration of industrial designs administered by WIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Proposed to make the Protocol more attractive by enabling Hague-system filings via ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: International industrial design applications under Hague (Section 5bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Defines 'Hague Agreement' and 'international application'; (2) An international application designating a Contracting State that is also bound by Hague shall be considered an application under this Protocol, Hague provisions apply alongside Protocol provisions, with Hague prevailing in conflict; (3) ARIPO Office may act as receiving Office for residents/nationals of Contracting States bound by Hague; (4) ARIPO shall act as designated Office in relation to such international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Sets out how Hague-system international applications are treated under the Protocol and ARIPO's roles as receiving and designated office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule on fees — Rules determine amounts and payment methods (New Section 5(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules relating to Fees shall determine in particular the amount of the fees and the ways in which they are to be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Delegates specification of fee amounts and payment mechanisms to the Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed form availability for filing (Amendment to Rule 5(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request shall be made on a printed form copies of which shall be obtainable from the ARIPO Office, ARIPO website or from any other electronic media and from the industrial property offices of Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Ensures standardized forms are accessible in print and electronically from ARIPO and national offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing and processing (New Rule 5bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents, industrial designs and utility model applications may be filed and processed in electronic form or by electronic means in accordance with the Administrative Instructions provided that the ARIPO Office or any Member State office shall permit paper filing; Administrative Instructions shall set out provisions/requirements for filing/processing electronic applications (acknowledgment, filing date procedures, physical requirements and consequences of non-compliance, signature/authentication, identity verification). No Member State is obliged to receive/process electronic filings unless it notifies ARIPO that it is prepared; a Member State that has notified may not refuse to process an electronic application that complies with Administrative Instructions. Rule 5bis applies mutatis mutandis to other correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Comprehensive framework for electronic filing, processing, and Member State notification/obligations; ensures interoperability while respecting Member State readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of utility models — industrial applicability (Amendment to Rule 18bis(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend Rule 18bis(2) so that novelty and industrial applicability (not inventive step) within the Contracting States of the Protocol shall be applied with respect to utility models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: For utility models, inventive step is not considered; only novelty and industrial applicability (with reference to local documentation) are applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion of reminder obligation for annual maintenance fees (Deletion of Rule 21(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete the obligation of the ARIPO Office to issue a reminder at least one month prior to the date on which an annual maintenance fee is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Removes Office's duty to remind applicants/owners to renew, aligning with other offices where applicants must monitor renewal dates themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications between ARIPO and national offices (Amendment to Rule 22(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications between the ARIPO Office and the industrial property offices of contracting states on matters relating to the Protocol and regulations shall be effected direct by registered mail or any other safe electronic means of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Introduces secure electronic communications as an acceptable means between ARIPO and designated states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Banjul Protocol — ARIPO role wording (Section 1:1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace wording 'administration' with 'management' of registered marks: ARIPO is entrusted with the registration of marks and the management of such registered marks on behalf of Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Users feel ARIPO 'manages' rather than 'administers' rights; wording change recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing transmission timing — late transmission filing date (Banjul Section 2:4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is filed with a national Industrial Property Office, that office shall, within one month of receiving the application, transmit it to the ARIPO Office; failure to do so means the application shall be accorded the date it is received at the ARIPO Office as the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Solves allocation of filing date when national offices delay transmission beyond one month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of goods/services and Nice Classification (Banjul Section 3:2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall indicate the goods and/or services (including the corresponding class(es) under the Nice Classification). ARIPO will check that class indication and, where missing or incorrect, classify the goods/services under the latest Nice edition upon payment of a classification fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Proposes using the latest Nice Classification edition for ARIPO applications and including a fee for ARIPO-performed classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive features — color, smell, sound (Banjul Section 3:3 amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where color, smell or sound is claimed to be a distinctive feature of the mark, the applicant shall make a statement to that effect, including names of colors and indication of principal parts; proposal is to extend to explicitly include smell and sound marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Aligns with international standards by recognizing smell and sound as possible distinctive features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date elements — minimum elements required (Banjul Section 3bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall accord as the filing date the date on which the following elements were received: (i) express or implied indication that registration is sought; (ii) indication allowing identity of applicant to be established; (iii) contact indications; (iv) clear reproduction of the mark; (v) list of goods/services. Amendment proposes removing 'some' and specifying minimum elements needed to accord a filing date as (i) and (ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Clarifies the minimum elements necessary to obtain a filing date, tightening the standard to at least indications (i) and (ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination time by designated states (Banjul Section 6:2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the expiration of twelve (proposed: nine) months from the date of notification under Section 5:3, each designated state may make a written communication that registered mark shall have no effect on its territory on any grounds (absolute/relative). Proposal reduces the period from 12 to 9 months (and potentially to 6 months after digitization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Reducing the examination period addresses user complaints about delays; further reduction expected after member state digitization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and renewal — registration period counted from priority date (Banjul Section 7:1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The registration of a mark shall be for a period of 10 years from the filing date (proposed amendment: change to 'priority date').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Aligns ARIPO practice with most jurisdictions and international standards where the 10-year term is computed from the priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and individual fee concept (Rule 10 amendments / new Rule 10.3 and 10.3.1/10.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 10.2 changed to include regional fees and introduce 'individual fees' for each designated state in line with the Madrid System. New Rule 10.3 allows a Contracting State to declare that, instead of a share in ARIPO fees, it will receive an individual fee specified in a declaration. Rule 10.3.1 requires notification of the Director General of the individual fee; Rule 10.3.2 caps the individual fee at the equivalent of what the State's Office would be entitled to in a national application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Designed to make the Banjul Protocol more attractive to Member States by allowing them to receive fees directly and match national fee structures; ARIPO requested member states to submit declarations of fee structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for adopting individual fee structure (Explanatory notes for Rule 10 changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only 9 of 18 Member States are party to the Banjul Protocol partly because national offices depend on revenue; adopting individual fee structures makes the Protocol financially more attractive and is envisioned to encourage accession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Administrative/political rationale accompanying the rule change, and description of outreach letters sent to Member States to adopt declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annex III — declaration template for individual fee structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Template declaration for a Contracting State to notify an individual fee under Rule 10.3 specifying amounts (US$) for application/subsequent designation and renewal per class and effective date; requires official stamp and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory Notes: Operational form to record a State's declared individual fee schedule and entry-into-force date.
